brief: The canvas displays an intricate, tabletop arrangement of cantilevered clockwork sculptures. These mechanisms are crafted entirely from polished brass and are designed to visualize the mathematical concept of orbital repetition. The style echoes the clean lines and functional aesthetics of 1920s Bauhaus design. The finished piece continuously animates, showing the delicate, rhythmic movement of linked, orbiting parts in perpetual motion.

statement: This sketch presents a mechanical universe of brass clockwork sculptures suspended in three-dimensional space, each component following its own orbital rhythm. The composition evokes the geometric precision and kinetic elegance of early 20th-century industrial design, where every rotating gear and cantilevered arm moves in harmony with mathematical precision. The viewer observes an endless dance of interlocking mechanisms, each one a testament to the beauty of repetitive motion and structured chaos. Through careful attention to lighting and material properties, the work suggests not just movement but the very essence of time itself as a series of ordered cycles.
